note_text: Apple is the first customer to adopt TSMC's 2nm process node. For the iPhone 18's A20 chips, Apple secured approximately half of the initial 2nm capacity, with volume production beginning in Q4 2025. https://www.macrumors.com/2025/08/28/apple-tsmc-2nm-production-iphone-18/ https://applemagazine.com/tsmc-2nm-chip-production-iphone-18/
claim: TSMC's 2 nm node is the first time Apple is not the first to adopt a new TSMC process node (excluding Huawei).
context: 2 nm is actually the first time they're not. Well, that's besides Huawei. Huawei, back in 2020 and before, was the first with Apple, but they were both making smartphones.

source_verification.reasoning: The note makes three claims: Apple is the first customer to adopt TSMC's 2nm node; Apple secured ~half of initial 2nm capacity for A20/iPhone 18; volume production began Q4 2025. The MacRumors source supports the half-capacity, Q4 2025 production, and A20/iPhone 18 claims. The AppleMagazine source supports the 'first major customer to adopt TSMC's 2nm node' claim. All factual claims are covered by good sources.

citations.quote: Apple has ordered almost half of TSMC's initial 2nm production capacity for the iPhone 18 as the pure foundry begins mass production of its next-generation chip process.
citations.explanation: Supports the claim that Apple secured approximately half of the initial 2nm capacity.

citations.quote: TSMC's 2nm process went into production in the fourth quarter of 2025 as planned
citations.explanation: Supports the Q4 2025 volume production claim.

citations.quote: the A20 chip in iPhone 18 models will be manufactured with TSMC's first-generation 2nm (N2) process
Apple is expected to be the first major customer to adopt TSMC’s 2nm node, with early chip production dedicated to the A20 Bionic processor, likely to debut in the iPhone 18 and iPhone 18 Pro models.
citations.explanation: Directly supports the claim that Apple is the first customer to adopt 2nm and ties it to A20/iPhone 18.
